node_definition.done_when: tests/test_landing_write_races_every_writer.py runs five writers — the landing record, a followup append, a section append, a state set and a comment append — each against an in-flight landing write on the same plan in a temporary repository. For each it asserts that the writer's change is present afterwards, or that its loss is refused with both versions named. A writer that still loses silently is repaired in reckon/_store.py or reckon/mcp.py until its case passes. The same file keeps §5's positive control: a sequential write still succeeds and advances the version. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
